card.name: "in" before a patient group
card.fires_on: The word "in" (or "among") right after a condition, symptom or risk, where a patient population comes next. Typical of warnings such as "muscle weakness in patients with...".

modes.label: Condition then "in"
modes.description: "in" follows a clinical problem and introduces the group who have it.
modes.example: Sleep apnea is common<< in>> MPS IVA patients.

modes.label: Risk then "in" or "among"
modes.description: The word follows a worsening or risk phrase and leads to a named patient group.
modes.example: GBCAs increase the risk for nephrogenic systemic fibrosis<< among>> patients with impaired elimination of the drugs.

card.writes: It pushes toward word starts that are not about people groups, and away from group words like homosexuals or carriers.
card.plain: It marks the little word "in" that introduces which patients a warning applies to.
